subject: Finova - Decision criteria clarification & stakeholder mapping
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finova.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: discovery + stakeholder mapping

Hi Sarah —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap and proposed next steps to keep momentum: 

1) Key decision criteria you shared: latency (P95 target), total cost per 1M tokens, deployment mode (private/VPC preferred), and SLA requirements for uptime & incident response.
2) Stakeholders we agreed to loop in: Security (for questionnaire), Procurement (PO/contract cadence), and the Product team (latency targets and perf validation).
3) Action items:
   - Sarah: confirm security questionnaire owner and procurement timeline (we discussed end of Q2).
   - Marissa: share mutual action plan (MAP) and example SLA language; schedule an ops/security walkthrough.
   - Marcus: field technical Qs on latency targets and deployment options.

I attached a draft Mutual Action Plan and example SLA wording for review. Can you confirm the internal stakeholders (names/emails) for security and procurement so we can include them on the MAP? Also, can you confirm if the deployment requirement is strictly private/VPC or if a Dedicated hosted option with specific region residency would be acceptable?

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0132

Attachments: Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx (spreadsheet), Example_SLA.txt

From: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-25T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery + stakeholder mapping

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the MAP. Quick answers:

- Security owner: Tom Alvarez (tom.alvarez@finova.com) — he owns third-party risk and will coordinate the questionnaire.
- Procurement: procurement@finova.com (primary contact is Elaine Park, but procurement@ will handle PO/legal routing).
- Product: I'll loop in Mike Reyes for perf validation (mike.reyes@finova.com).

On deployment: our preference is Private (VPC) for initial rollouts due to PII residency concerns, but we're open to Dedicated hosted in a US-only region if the residency controls and SLA match.

Latency / cost: The stakeholders are targeting P95 generation latency under ~150ms for 256-token responses during steady-state peak, and total cost not to exceed $0.0009/token for inference compute (we understand tradeoffs with quantization). We'll confirm exact numbers after internal perf review.

Timeline: Security questionnaire needs to be completed by mid-May to make the Q2 procurement window.

I'll loop Tom and procurement on the thread.

Thanks,
Sarah
Director, Product Integrations | Finova

From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finova.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-26T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery + stakeholder mapping

Thanks Sarah — tagging in a few clarifying technical questions so we can size the perf work: 

1) When you say P95 < 150ms for 256 tokens, is that measured end-to-end from API call to final token, including network hops, or is that server-side generation time only?
2) Expected concurrency/throughput at peak (RPS or concurrent requests) for initial rollout? That will determine whether Dedicated capacity or a Private VPC with autoscaling is the better fit.
3) Are you planning for synchronous generation (single API call) or streaming responses for the user experience?

If you prefer, we can run a quick perf test with a small workload on our Dedicated environment to collect baseline numbers and iterate.

Cheers,
Marcus
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus@redwood.com

From: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finova.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finova.com>
Cc: procurement@finova.com
Date: 2028-03-27T10:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery + stakeholder mapping

Hi all —

Thanks for the details. A few clarifications from Security/Procurement side:

- Security: we'll treat latency targets as end-to-end for the user flow — but for procurement/SOC review we need the server-side P95 and details on network egress controls (VPC endpoints, private peering).
- Deployment: Private VPC is preferred for initial rollout. If Redwood can support Bring-Your-Own-Key (BYOK) and region-restricted tenancy (US-only), Dedicated hosted could be considered later.
- SLA: We expect 99.9% uptime for production endpoints and a documented incident response plan with RTO/RPO guidance.

Perf numbers: initial expected peak is ~50 concurrent sessions (avg. 2 RPS per session) with burst to ~150 concurrent during batch processing windows. We can share a sample workload trace offline.

Procurement: attaching our PO template and the high-level security requirements doc. We aim to have contract terms finalized by the end of May if the security review finishes mid-May.

Attachments: Finova_Security_Requirements.pdf (PDF), Finova_PO_Template.docx (Word)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Tom Alvarez <tom.alvarez@finova.com>, Sarah Chen <sarah.chen@finova.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, procurement@finova.com
Date: 2028-03-28T15:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: discovery + stakeholder mapping

Tom / Sarah —

Thanks for the clarity and the attachments, Tom. Quick recap + proposed plan:

- Deployment: We will prioritize Private VPC for the initial rollout. Our Private offering supports VPC peering and region restrictions; BYOK is available via KMS integration (we'll include the integration doc in the security call).
- Latency targets: We'll treat the P95 < 150ms as end-to-end for product acceptance but will provide server-side P95 baselines and network architecture diagrams in the security packet.
- SLA: Redwood offers SLA wording similar to 99.9% uptime and an incident response runbook. I'll share the example SLA we discussed and flag any procurement redlines to you by next week.
- Perf validation: Marcus will run a short Dedicated perf test (or simulated load in Private) to capture server-side P95 for 256-token prompts. Marcus: can you propose two windows next week for a 60-minute perf run?
- Security walkthrough: proposing 2028-04-10 or 2028-04-12 for a 60-minute questionnaire walk-through with Tom and the security team. Please confirm availability.
- Procurement: We'll review your PO template and send a redlined version by 2028-04-05.

Next steps (summary):
   * Marcus to schedule perf run & share baseline numbers.
   * Marissa to share MAP link, SLA example, and BYOK integration doc to this thread.
   * Tom/Sarah to confirm questionnaire attendees and procurement contact details.

Links/attachments: https://drive.google.com/finova/mutual-action-plan (MAP), Example_SLA.txt, BYOK_integration_guide.pdf

If that works, I'll schedule the security walkthrough and the perf run once Marcus confirms times.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: Mutual_Action_Plan.xlsx, Example_SLA.txt, BYOK_integration_guide.pdf
